title: Locality-aware Fair Scheduling in LLM Serving
technique: Deficit Longest Prefix Match (DLPM) and Double Deficit LPM (D2LPM): per-client deficit counters that bound service difference while preserving prefix-cache locality and load balance

optimized_metrics.evidence: our goal is to achieve approximate max-min fairness on the service received by each client; different from VTC, we also want to preserve prefix cache locality
ensuring fairness while maintaining high throughput (up to 2.87x higher than VTC)
We assess the scheduler's effectiveness in maintaining service quality for well-behaved clients by measuring their P50 and P99 latency.
DLPM ... can maintain a high degree of prefix locality with a fairness guarantee

headline_claim.text: ensuring fairness while maintaining high throughput (up to 2.87x higher than VTC) and low per-client (up to 7.18x lower than state-of-the-art distributed LLM serving system) latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We measure the clients' service as a weighted sum of the number of input tokens and the number of output tokens, following VTC [42]. ... the weight for input token is 1 and the weight for output token is 2.

J = (sum x_i)^2 / (n sum x_i^2) ... we compute the Jain's Fairness Index by letting x_i denote the service rate of client i. The calculation is based on the time interval during which all clients are active
We measure latency using the end-to-end completion time for program evaluation. We use the TTFT (Time to First Token) latency metric for long-context QA tasks.
metric_definitions.notes: latency of well-behaved clients only; program completion for ToT/LLM-judge, TTFT for long-context QA; TTFT never otherwise defined

load_regime: Gamma-process synthetic client traces, request rate scaled with GPUs, two misbehaving-client patterns (S1 more requests, S2 longer prefix); real multi-turn chat trace re-scaled
tradeoff_acknowledged: fairness competes with throughput (Pareto frontier vs LPM); D2LPM loses throughput on long-context QA with 8 GPUs because cache hit rate drops from 95% to 50%
workloads: Long-Context QA, Tree-of-Thoughts, LLM-as-Judge synthetic; real multi-turn chat
extractor_notes: Ambiguous objective: fairness (guaranteed bound) is the primary design goal, throughput/locality and per-client latency are co-objectives; paper frames it as navigating a fairness-locality Pareto frontier.
